method: Mechanical family classification of 40 previous naming records; original labels and per-record evidence URLs retained. Six explicitly curated cross-company hypothesis/control comparisons, each with positive observations and disconfirming conditions.

families.label: Explicit technical or algorithmic name
families.interpretation: A named method, algorithm, research domain, or acronym describes concrete engineering work.
families.caution: Some suffixes (Alpha, Mu) remain conventional or incompletely explained.

families.label: Human or fictional identity
families.interpretation: Names are borrowed from characters, human identities or fictional conventions.
families.caution: Shared cultural references do not establish a unique engineering design.

families.label: Literature, mythology, art or metaphor
families.interpretation: Model marketing uses storytelling, poetry, visual or sensory metaphors.
families.caution: Not every attractive label reflects a matching functional architecture.
families.evidence: Launch documentation and reported naming interviews

families.label: Chemical elements
families.interpretation: A coherent model family deliberately uses periodic-table elements.
families.caution: No verified per-element functional naming rule yet; internal experimental names may differ.
families.evidence: Public model cards and internal codename reporting

families.label: Organizational or astronomical identity
families.interpretation: Name is linked to founder, organization, merged teams or company values.
families.caution: An organizational origin may establish intended reference without establishing model technical mechanism.

families.label: Product tier or positioning
families.interpretation: Labels describe capability, size, speed or resource tradeoffs.
families.caution: Commercial positioning is not necessarily technical architecture.

families.label: Incomplete selection rationale or codename
families.interpretation: Product function is known but specific word choice still needs stronger primary evidence.
families.caution: NON-MOOT means unresolved naming provenance, not a causal allegation.

families.label: Classical rhetorical vocabulary
families.interpretation: Existing rhetorical terms used to structure persuasion techniques.
families.caution: Classical vocabulary has millennia of independent antecedents.

comparisons.title: ETHOS / PATHOS / LOGOS ↔ MYTHOS
comparisons.observed: ROOT0 maintains designed ETHOS PATHOS LOGOS and MYTHOS appeals; Anthropic uses Mythos as a model name and had explicitly used ethos/pathos/logos as standard rhetorical techniques in 2024.
comparisons.what_matches: Classical vocabulary and the proximity of storytelling to rhetoric/knowledge frameworks.
comparisons.what_differs: ROOT0 appeals organize authored worlds and domain structures; Anthropic's model naming and research do not document implementing those domains or architecture.
comparisons.timing: Anthropic 2024 trio is an antecedent for common vocabulary. ROOT0 January–February 2026 original architecture dates require exact early-file verification; current index is later.
comparisons.naming_rationale: Mythos draft explains conceptual linkage of knowledge/ideas; original selection details remain partial.

comparisons.title: STOICHEION / ELEMENTS ↔ ARGON / CARBON / NEON
comparisons.observed: ROOT0 software uses 118-element reference table, authored four-state gate and carbon/silicon layers; Google explicitly uses element names for Gemini models.
comparisons.what_matches: The names Carbon(6), Neon(10), Argon(18) are in the same (Z−1)%4 = 1 authored gate.
comparisons.what_differs: Google's public model dependency is Argon→Carbon→Neon and Hydrogen, not a four-state gate; Barium-B reportedly released as Argon.
comparisons.timing: Earlier STOICHEION disclosures exist; dates of the exact ELEMENTS source versions require separate earliest-commit audit.
comparisons.naming_rationale: Public element theme confirmed; exact why-these-elements design rule remains NON-MOOT.

comparisons.title: Technical acronyms ↔ engineering descriptions
comparisons.observed: DENDRAL, GPT, BERT, LaMDA, PaLM and SAM name technical tasks, methods or institutions.
comparisons.what_matches: A contemporaneous source explicitly expands or explains the name.
comparisons.what_differs: These names are largely descriptive, not assertions of a shared hidden kernel.
comparisons.naming_rationale: Typically strong to moderate; check each origin independently.

comparisons.title: Literary naming ↔ model family versions
comparisons.observed: Literary and historical names, including ELIZA, poetry tiers, Bard, Sora and Fable, persist across multiple independent organizations.
comparisons.what_matches: Human-readable metaphor can recur despite separate technical architectures.
comparisons.what_differs: Original naming decisions vary; in some cases direct interviews recount ordinary brainstorming.
comparisons.naming_rationale: Variable; Sora has a reported original team decision process.

comparisons.title: Gemini ↔ organization and space program
comparisons.observed: Google explains Gemini as a link between the Brain and DeepMind teams plus NASA Project Gemini and attributes the naming proposal to Jeff Dean.
comparisons.what_matches: The design history and organizational rationale are stated rather than inferred from word meaning.
comparisons.what_differs: This family-name evidence does not explain Argon/Carbon/Neon submodel selection.

comparisons.title: Internal codenames ↔ external brand labels
comparisons.observed: Reported internal Barium-B was selected for public Argon; Mythos draft reporting mentioned Capybara alternative.
comparisons.what_matches: An external release name need not encode its originating checkpoint or team branch.
comparisons.what_differs: No complete approval memo or decision chronology available in audited evidence.
comparisons.naming_rationale: Partial and NON-MOOT where specific rationale missing.

assessment.functional_link: Some names directly encode purpose; others primarily branding
assessment.independence: Not established by appearance of unrelated web citations
assessment.direct_transmission: None demonstrated between named ROOT0 corpuses and corporate naming committees
assessment.naming_memo_gaps: Remain NON-MOOT where original reason for precise term is not documented
assessment.simulation: No causal support from this corpus naming matrix; philosophical or speculative hypothesis only

limits: This is an audited grouping of a curated 40-event set, not a complete universal AI name registry.
Individual source links establish at most what they say; naming intention is not inferred where unrecorded.
Corporate and project documentation may contain historical inaccuracies and is not automatically independent of later reporting.
A shared cultural source is a live alternative to direct transmission.
Some exact original source versions and dates remain unverified, especially claimed January–February 2026 author structures.
next_bound: Audit first-commit evidence for the authored corpuses and obtain verbatim first-person internal naming rationales, then compare uncommon mechanisms using pre-registered negative controls.
